item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q026_protein_kinase_like_function_transfer","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08 these catalytic domains are grouped in class d, Alpha and beta proteins (a+b), fold d.144 Protein kinase-like (PK-like), and superfamily d.144.1 Protein kinase-like (PK-like). That superfamily placement is stronger than a fold-only resemblance: it supports probable homology of the catalytic core and transfer of only coarse mechanistic features, such as a PK-like ATP-binding/phosphoryl-transfer scaffold. The three named activities are different families under that same superfamily: phosphoinositide 3-kinase catalytic domains are family d.144.1.4, sunid 56171; APH aminoglycoside phosphotransferases are family d.144.1.6, sunid 64411; canonical protein-kinase catalytic subunits are family d.144.1.7, sunid 88854. Representative PI3K, APH, and protein-kinase domains d4ps3a4, d1j7ia_, and d2pe0a_ likewise meet only at the PK-like superfamily node, so none of them is in the same SCOPe family as either of the others. Do not transfer protein-substrate recognition, aminoglycoside recognition, phosphoinositide lipid specificity, activation-loop behavior, regulatory-subunit contacts, membrane recruitment, or inhibitor selectivity merely from this shared scaffold. Those claims need family/orthology-level sequence evidence plus residue-level conservation of catalytic and substrate-binding sites, structures or alignments covering the relevant loops and regulatory surfaces, ligand/substrate or regulator complexes where available, and direct biochemical or mutational data showing the same specificity or regulation. For template choice, the shared superfamily can justify a remote catalytic-core template, but divergent insertions, termini, substrate pockets, and allosteric interfaces should be treated as unmodeled or low-confidence unless supported by close homologs or experimental structures.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope.get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope.search_scop: /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=PI3K&mode=auto&limit=20; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=aminoglycoside+phosphotransferase&mode=auto&limit=20","mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.144; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.144/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.144.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.144.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56171; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56171/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/64411; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/64411/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/88854; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/88854/parents","mcp__scope.list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.144.1/children?limit=50","mcp__scope.compare_scop_domains: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d4ps3a4; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d4ps3a4/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1j7ia_; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1j7ia_/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d2pe0a_; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d2pe0a_/parents"]}]}
